correctness.rationale: For every invertible real planar matrix with distinct singular values, SVD reduces the expected rank-one projector to two equiprobable orthogonal sketch direction pairs. The trace-one Bloch discriminant equals \(r^2[(uv)^2+(1-r^2)(t-u^2)^2]/[(1-r^2v^2)(1-r^2u^2)]\) exactly for all real parameters. Positive denominators and \(0<r<1\) give the unique global optimum \(t=u^2\) on \([0,1]\). The update for \(A^\top x=b\) is precisely \((I-P_s)e\), and the least eigenvalue gives the largest uniform geometric contraction coefficient, with equality for the least-eigenvector at one step. Conditioning independent sign entries on a nonzero outcome yields \(t=p/(2-p)\). Boundary alignments and equal-singular-value exception are explicit. All 1152 direct rational projector/discriminant/checker identities passed by standalone `verify.py`; this is supplemental to the proof.

originality.rationale: Published work establishes both the general sketch-and-project projector contraction and a convex semidefinite optimization of arbitrary finite-sketch probabilities (Gower–Richtárik Section 5.1) and estimates expected projections for Gaussian, Rademacher and LESS sketches. The precise claim here optimizes the entire conditioned Bernoulli sign-density continuum for arbitrary planar singular directions and finds a unique orientation-only optimum, with a strict interior improvement. The inspected full-text source statements and comparison results do not imply that finite-dimensional optimization law. Exact equivalences and stronger possible coverage were checked; residual risk remains from unindexed specialized derivations and the simplicity of the planar algebra.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis, short note, or special-case exercise may already derive the same four-direction mixed projector identity.
The optimum requires right singular-vector orientation; its computational acquisition cost and high-dimensional behavior are not analyzed.
Search and available full-text review cannot establish global priority or independence of the result.

The closed-form planar optimum is a specialization of a known general discrete probability SDP, so priority and value depend on the nontriviality and utility of the exact new evaluation, not on the optimization framework itself.

value.rationale: The Bernoulli density is a natural actionable parameter controlling number of nonzeros in a standard sign sketch, and the smallest-eigenvalue objective is the exact uniform error guarantee of an established linear solver. The result is a complete real-parameter classification for every invertible planar anisotropic matrix, not an isolated numerical witness or a rescaled previous bound. The optimizer is strictly interior at generic angles and unexpectedly independent of spectral condition despite the achieved rate depending on it; at \(\kappa=2\) and \(\theta=\pi/8\) it improves the sharp coefficient from \((1-3/\sqrt{41})/2\) at both endpoints to \(13/41\). A complete two-dimensional benchmark is meaningful even without a downstream high-dimensional theorem or wall-time guarantee.
